chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Bashir al-Dahan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was ill with the illness in which he died, he sent for Ali (peace be upon him). When Ali came, he leaned over him and kept speaking to him and he kept speaking to him. When he came out, they met him and said to him: 'What did your companion tell you?' He said: 'He told me of a gate that opens a thousand gates, each of which opens a thousand gates.'

key_terms.أَكَبَّ عَلَيْهِ: He leaned over him / bowed towards him
key_terms.مَرَضَهُ الَّذِي تُوُفِّيَ فِيهِ: The illness in which he died

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet tell Ali during his final illness according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recounts the Prophet’s final private counsel to Ali (peace be upon him), where the metaphor of a 'gate opening into a thousand gates' signifies the vast, hierarchical depth of divine knowledge (*Ilm*) and authority (*Wilayah*) entrusted to the Ahl al-Bayt. This imagery underscores the Shia belief that the Imams possess the esoteric interpretation (*Ta'wil*) of the Quran, serving as the living keys to its infinite layers of meaning.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-18 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Abdullah ibn Amer ibn Sa’ed, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, on the authority of Safvan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Bashir al-Dahan that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“When the Prophet (MGB) was so ill that he (MGB) was about to die, he asked for Ali (MGB) and once Ali (MGB) came in, the Prophet (MGB) whispered things in his ears. When Ali (MGB) came out, they (i.e. Abu Bakr and Umar) asked Ali (MGB), “What did your friend (MGB) tell you?” Ali (MGB) said, “He taught me one gate which opens up to one-thousand gates each of which opens up to another one-thousand gates.”
